# RG17 `unevidenced-setup`: The test builds a counterparty the evidence does not cover

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** warn (warn; silenced for a name listed under deployment.evidence)

The test deploys a stand-in (a strategy, a malicious target, a hook) or calls `ship`, `dock` or `push` on a protocol contract, and `deployment.evidence` in realism.yaml does not name that contract or that actor.

## Why it matters

A local `new Protocol()` is a normal harness and is not this rule. What this rule is for is the behavior the test invents on top of it: a maker strategy nobody's deployment ships, a dock, a push performed outside the path the protocol's own docs allow, a malicious target the test wrote. The profit then depends on a counterparty the test created. The tool cannot read those docs. `deployment.evidence` is where the author cites the deployment address, the config, and the page a reader can check. A missing citation is the finding.

## How to fix it

Cite the deployment under `deployment.evidence` with the contract or actor name, the address, the config, and a source a reader can open. If there is no such deployment, the report has to say the behavior is one the test constructed.

## Fires on

```solidity
vm.prank(maker);
aqua.ship(address(router), abi.encode(order), tokens, amounts);
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
vm.prank(attacker);
vault.deposit(1e18, attacker);
```

## How it can be wrong

- A contract the attacker deploys as their own (`MaliciousToken`, an exploit helper). The name matches a stand-in, and on the labelled 0.5.0 sample this was most of the flags. The attacker could have deployed it. An `allow` comment is the silence.
- A permissionless `ship` or `push` that any user can do, and that real users do. The rule cannot read the docs that say so. An evidence entry, or an `allow` comment citing the page, is the record.
- `array.push` on a memory array is not flagged; only a call on a contract the harness treats as the protocol. A helper the tool misreads as the protocol will be flagged. Helpers defined in the test's own file are not protocol contracts.
- The evidence entry is trusted, not checked. A citation that names the wrong deployment silences the rule and is visible in realism.yaml for the triager to read.

## In Solana tests (Rust and Anchor TypeScript)

Not checked. Solana tests are not checked for unevidenced setup. A privileged signer in the exploit is RG02.

## In Move tests (Sui and Aptos)

Not checked. Move tests are not checked for unevidenced setup. There is no `deployment.evidence` match against Move calls yet.

## Silencing it

An `allow` comment in the repo under review does not silence this rule, and neither does a `realism.yaml` or `realism-gate.toml` inside that repo. Policy is an operator file outside the tree (`--declaration`, `--config`). `--trust-inline-allows` is the author switch, for a PoC you wrote and are not gating.

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG17) <why this is not a defect here>
```

The comment is the same in Rust, TypeScript and Move. A comment without a reason is ignored even with `--trust-inline-allows`, and the output says so.
